topics.summary: On November 20, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann hypothesis as a 17-million-line Lean library, made working with Claude, and the Lean and Mathlib communities certified it as correct the next day.
topics.why_now: Two attempts landed the same day: Alpöge's machine-checked proof, and a 940-page human-written manuscript by Alessandro Masullo aimed at the generalized hypothesis, which readers have since found gaps in. The Hacker News thread on Masullo's announcement drew 2,447 points.

editorial.brief: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO ran across five feeds at once, from 2,396 points on Hacker News to a stock rally on the wire. Polymarket put $2M of 24-hour volume behind a new Nvidia CEO being named by year end, priced at 100 percent. Wikipedia's top article, Ramayana: Part 1, has no such company.
editorial.cover_sub: Ramayana: Part 1 led Wikipedia with 365,685 views, 1.4 times the runner-up, on a day when the cross-feed story belonged to Nvidia and no other feed mentioned it.
editorial.wiki_deck: Ramayana: Part 1 drew 365,685 views, well ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI. The snapshot offers no reason for it, which makes it the day's one clean mystery.
editorial.letter_headline: One loud story and a great deal of routine
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is absorbed in Nvidia and new software, Lemmy is irritated with Washington, Bluesky splits between a Chicago walkout and old film nostalgia, and Mastodon is dry about bot checks.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire stuck to Huang's return and the Asian stock rally behind it, while searchers looked up UAE against India A, the beaver moon, Lakers-Jazz and Bolsa Familia.
editorial.markets_deck: A new Nvidia CEO by year end sits at 100 percent on $2M, a Fed hold at 3 percent, and the rest is Counter-Strike plus one Yokohama match at $3M.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,092,874 players on Steam, ahead of Dota 2 at 772,488 and PUBG at 751,809, while on Twitch caseoh_ has 74,039 viewers and TheBurntPeanut has 44,337.
editorial.yt_note: The trailer's 33,175,150 views dwarf everything else, including two Travis Scott uploads from the GTA VI album and a 10,000-player Minecraft war at 2,136,376.
editorial.closing_note: The 2,396 Hacker News points, the beaver moon search and the Avengers trailer count will all have moved on by tomorrow's edition. Ramayana: Part 1 will either hold its place or return to the pages nobody checks. Grand Theft Auto VI will still be coming.
wiki_paras: Ramayana: Part 1 took the top spot on Wikipedia with 365,685 views, ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI on 266,240. That is a lead of 1.4 times over second place, comfortable but not a rout. Jensen Huang follows on 234,343, with Moon and The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping close behind at about 180,000 each.

Nothing else in the snapshot accounts for it. No cluster, no matching headline, no Google Trends entry, no trending video carries the name. Whatever produced those 365,685 views did so out of sight of the other sixteen feeds. The data offers no cause, and a cause invented to fill the gap would be worse than the gap.

The more crowded story sits just behind it. Grand Theft Auto VI and Jensen Huang hold second and third, and both turn up elsewhere in the snapshot, the first on YouTube and Google Trends, the second on five feeds. The top of Wikipedia today is one unexplained name followed by two the other feeds can explain.
letter_paras: Today is a single-story day with a long quiet tail. Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO appeared on Bluesky, the AI wire, Hacker News, Lemmy and Wikipedia, and Hacker News gave it 2,396 points. Grand Theft Auto VI supplied a smaller second story across Wikipedia, YouTube and Google Trends. Almost everything else in the snapshot kept to its own corner.

Hugging Face lists inworld/voice-isolator at 0 downloads, while the GGUF build of Inkling-2-Mini sits at 1,292,888. Hacker News has Drone Maps of Salvage Yards on 31 points. A Mastodon user is considering a static page that reads Verifying you are human. The USGS logged 25 quakes of M2.5 or above, the largest M5.5 west of Macquarie Island.

Same-hour snapshots are useful because nobody has had time to rewrite them. By next week the Nvidia story will have a settled account and the Ramayana figure will have an explanation, or will not. Today there are only counts, taken side by side. Kept daily, the quiet days become the baseline that makes the loud ones measurable.
